primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Chronic irritant exposure causes mucus gland enlargement, goblet-cell hyperplasia, and chronic productive cough with airflow obstruction.
vignette: A 62-year-old smoker has a productive cough for most days during at least 3 months in each of the past 2 years.
distractor_notes: Emphysema is defined by alveolar wall destruction and may have little cough.
Asthma is episodic and reversible.
Bronchiectasis causes permanently dilated bronchi with recurrent infections and copious sputum.
IPF causes restrictive dry cough and crackles.
key_expl: The clinical definition of chronic bronchitis is productive cough for at least 3 months in 2 consecutive years.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Protease-antiprotease imbalance and oxidant injury destroy alveolar walls, enlarge distal airspaces, reduce elastic recoil, and promote expiratory airway collapse.
vignette: A 68-year-old smoker has hyperinflated lungs, decreased breath sounds, and low DLCO.
lead: Which mechanical change most directly causes air trapping?
correct: Loss of elastic recoil of alveolar walls
distractor_notes: Elastic recoil is reduced, not increased.
Surfactant deficiency causes alveolar collapse and restrictive physiology.
Pleural fluid causes compression and restriction.
Bronchial smooth muscle is more central to asthma.
key_expl: Alveolar wall destruction reduces elastic recoil and radial traction, causing expiratory collapse and air trapping.

sources.support: NHLBI describes emphysema as alveolar destruction with impaired exhalation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes granulomatous pulmonary infection that can present with chronic cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss, and upper-lobe cavitation.
vignette: A 44-year-old man has 2 months of cough, night sweats, weight loss, and hemoptysis. Chest imaging shows an apical cavitary lesion.
lead: Which immune structure is most characteristic of the host response to this infection?
correct: Caseating granuloma formed by activated macrophages and T cells
distractor_notes: Noncaseating granulomas are more typical of sarcoidosis.
Eosinophilic inflammation is associated with allergy and parasites.
Acute pyogenic abscesses are not the classic TB response.
Linear basement-membrane injury describes anti-GBM disease.
key_expl: Cell-mediated immunity to M tuberculosis produces granulomas that often develop central caseous necrosis.
objective: Identify the characteristic granulomatous immune response in tuberculosis.

sources.support: CDC describes pulmonary TB symptoms including cough, hemoptysis, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Profound T-cell immunodeficiency predisposes to diffuse Pneumocystis infection causing nonproductive cough, fever, hypoxemia, and bilateral interstitial opacities.
vignette: A patient with untreated HIV and CD4 count 90/µL has fever, progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities.
lead: Which organism is most likely responsible?
distractor_notes: S pneumoniae more often causes focal lobar pneumonia.
Mycoplasma causes atypical pneumonia in generally immunocompetent younger patients.
Legionella often causes systemic features and hyponatremia.
Aspergillus disease has different patterns including nodules, cavitation, or fungal balls.
key_expl: Advanced HIV with diffuse hypoxemic interstitial pneumonia strongly suggests Pneumocystis jirovecii.
clues: dry cough and diffuse ground-glass opacities

sources.support: NIAID describes advanced HIV as causing severe immune deficiency and opportunistic infections.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Small cell lung cancer is a central neuroendocrine carcinoma strongly associated with smoking and may produce ectopic ACTH or ADH.
vignette: A heavy smoker has a central hilar lung mass, weight loss, and hyponatremia from SIADH.
lead: Which histologic type is most likely?
distractor_notes: Adenocarcinoma is often peripheral and less tightly linked to paraneoplastic SIADH.
Squamous carcinoma can be central and cause PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia.
Large cell carcinoma lacks the classic neuroendocrine SIADH association.
Mesothelioma is pleural and linked to asbestos.
key_expl: A central smoking-related neuroendocrine tumor with SIADH is classic small cell lung cancer.
objective: Associate small cell lung cancer with SIADH.

sources.title: Small Cell Lung Cancer
sources.support: NCI describes small cell lung carcinoma as a smoking-associated neuroendocrine lung cancer.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Smoking-related squamous carcinoma often arises centrally and can secrete PTH-related peptide, causing humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy.
vignette: A 65-year-old smoker has a central cavitary lung mass and hypercalcemia with suppressed endogenous PTH.
lead: Which tumor-produced factor most likely explains the hypercalcemia?
distractor_notes: Calcitonin lowers serum calcium.
EPO causes erythrocytosis, not hypercalcemia.
Aldosterone regulates sodium and potassium.
IGF-1 mediates growth hormone effects.
key_expl: Squamous cell lung carcinoma can secrete PTHrP, causing hypercalcemia with low native PTH.

sources.title: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
sources.support: NCI describes squamous cell carcinoma as a major NSCLC subtype.

sources.title: Hypercalcemia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes malignancy-related hypercalcemia.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Podocyte foot-process effacement causes selective albuminuria and nephrotic syndrome, especially in children; light microscopy is often normal.
vignette: A 5-year-old child has edema, heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and normal complement. Light microscopy is normal.
distractor_notes: FSGS more often affects older patients and shows segmental sclerosis on light microscopy.
PSGN is nephritic with hematuria and low complement.
IgA nephropathy causes recurrent hematuria.
Alport syndrome causes hereditary hematuria with hearing abnormalities.
key_expl: Childhood nephrotic syndrome with normal light microscopy is classic minimal change disease.

sources.title: Nephrotic Syndrome in Children
sources.support: NIDDK describes minimal change disease as a common cause of childhood nephrotic syndrome.

sources.title: Minimal change disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes nephrotic syndrome with minimal light-microscopic change.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Podocyte injury causes focal and segmental glomerular scarring and nephrotic syndrome, associated with HIV, obesity, reduced nephron mass, and certain genetic variants.
vignette: An adult with HIV develops nephrotic-range proteinuria. Kidney biopsy shows sclerosis affecting portions of some glomeruli.
distractor_notes: Minimal change disease lacks segmental sclerosis on light microscopy.
Membranous nephropathy shows diffuse capillary wall thickening.
IgA nephropathy is primarily nephritic with mesangial IgA.
PSGN follows infection and is nephritic with low complement.
key_expl: Focal segmental sclerosis in a patient with HIV and nephrotic syndrome supports FSGS.
objective: Recognize FSGS from biopsy pattern and associations.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes FSGS as glomerular scarring causing proteinuria.

sources.support: NIDDK describes FSGS among causes of adult nephrotic syndrome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Subepithelial immune deposits along glomerular capillary walls activate complement and injure podocytes, causing nephrotic proteinuria.
vignette: A 52-year-old man has nephrotic syndrome. Biopsy shows diffuse capillary-wall thickening with subepithelial immune deposits.
lead: Where are the deposits located relative to the glomerular basement membrane?
correct: Between the basement membrane and podocytes
distractor_notes: Subendothelial deposits occur in several nephritic immune-complex disorders.
Mesangial deposits characterize IgA nephropathy.
Bowman's space is not the classic immune-deposit site.
Tubular intracellular deposits do not define membranous nephropathy.
key_expl: Membranous nephropathy is characterized by subepithelial deposits beneath podocytes.
objective: Localize immune deposits in membranous nephropathy.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes membranous nephropathy as an immune-mediated cause of nephrotic syndrome.

sources.support: NIDDK describes membranous nephropathy among adult nephrotic causes.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Reduced renal perfusion with intact tubular function increases sodium and water reabsorption, often yielding low urine sodium and low fractional excretion of sodium.
vignette: A patient with severe volume depletion has rising creatinine, urine sodium 8 mEq/L, and concentrated urine.
lead: Which mechanism best explains the low urine sodium?
correct: Intact tubular sodium reabsorption in response to low renal perfusion
distractor_notes: ATN impairs sodium reabsorption and tends to increase urine sodium.
Aldosterone deficiency would increase sodium loss.
Osmotic diuresis increases urinary solute and water loss.
Proximal transport failure causes solute wasting.
key_expl: In prerenal AKI, functioning tubules avidly retain sodium to preserve effective volume.
objective: Explain low urine sodium in prerenal AKI.
clues: low urine sodium with concentrated urine

sources.support: NIDDK describes low blood flow to kidneys as a major AKI mechanism.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Ischemic or nephrotoxic tubular epithelial injury causes cell sloughing, granular casts, impaired concentrating ability, and intrinsic AKI.
vignette: After prolonged septic shock, a patient develops rising creatinine and muddy brown granular casts in urine.
distractor_notes: Prerenal azotemia has intact tubules and bland sediment.
AIN often has pyuria, WBC casts, rash, fever, or eosinophilia.
Postrenal obstruction requires urinary tract blockage.
Minimal change disease causes nephrotic proteinuria.
key_expl: Muddy brown granular casts after ischemic injury are classic ATN.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes ischemic and toxic tubular injury causing intrinsic AKI.

sources.title: Acute Kidney Injury
sources.support: NIDDK describes intrinsic kidney injury as a cause of AKI.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Drug-triggered hypersensitivity inflammation of the renal interstitium and tubules can cause AKI with fever, rash, eosinophilia, pyuria, and WBC casts.
vignette: A patient develops fever, diffuse rash, eosinophilia, and rising creatinine 10 days after starting a beta-lactam antibiotic. Urine has WBC casts.
distractor_notes: ATN is associated with muddy brown casts rather than hypersensitivity features.
PSGN causes red-cell casts and nephritic syndrome.
Prerenal azotemia has bland sediment.
Renal artery stenosis causes renovascular hypertension and chronic perfusion issues.
key_expl: Drug exposure plus fever, rash, eosinophilia, and WBC casts is classic AIN.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Reduced phosphate excretion and reduced renal calcitriol production lower ionized calcium and stimulate parathyroid hormone secretion in chronic kidney disease.
vignette: A patient with advanced chronic kidney disease has high phosphate, low-normal calcium, and markedly elevated PTH.
lead: Which renal defect contributes most directly to the low calcitriol level?
distractor_notes: Intestinal tissue does not perform the key renal activation step.
Hepatic 25-hydroxylation precedes renal activation and is not the major CKD defect.
Parathyroid glands do not synthesize systemic calcitriol.
Skin melanin affects vitamin D synthesis from sunlight but does not explain advanced CKD physiology.
key_expl: The kidney converts 25-hydroxyvitamin D to active 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D using 1-alpha-hydroxylase.
